newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, hi-techs lead.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, hi-techs lead.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London pushed slightly higher on Wednesday, lifted by interest in high technology shares, but dealers said upside potential was limited after a lacklustre performance on Wall Street overnight.
"The Street looked a bit tired yesterday but with T-bonds and futures a bit better today we might see it gain perhaps 10 points today," one dealer said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed over 6,000 points but quickly reversed early gains to end at 5,966.77, down 13.04 points on the day, as profit-taking and worries about third-quarter earnings killed momentum.
In London, dealers said the underlying tone remained firm but that little major movement was expected ahead of Friday's U.S. retail sales and producer prices data.
"Hi-techs look a fraction higher today on the book-to-bill figures but otherwise it's very quiet," one trader said.

The U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association said on Tuesday the North American book-to-bill ratio rose to 0.99 in September from a revised 0.93 in August. The ratio means manufacturers received $99 in new orders for every $100 in shipments.
Among gainers in London, Intel was up $2.0 at $103-1/2 and Texas was up $5/8 at $55-3/4.
Micron gained $3/4 to $32-1/4 and Motorola, which dropped sharply in New York after it reported a fall in third quarter earnings, bounced back slightly to trade $1/4 higher at $48-3/4, traders said.
